overview:
Yuba County CA SO uses Flock Safety technology to capture objective evidence without compromising on individual privacy. Yuba County CA SO utilizes retroactive search to solve crimes after they've occurred. Additionally, Yuba County CA SO utilizes real time alerting of hotlist vehicles to capture wanted criminals. In an effort to ensure proper usage and guardrails are in place, they have made the below policies and usage statistics available to the public.

Adherence to Key Privacy Principles

Built to focus on data minimization, purpose limitation, and transparency.

Myth vs. Fact
Myth

Flock has been hacked.

Fact

Flock's cloud environment has never been breached. Flock invests in a strong security posture, including adhering to NDAA, SOC2 (Type II), ISO 27001, ISO 27018 FedRAMP 20x, and Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Tool (HECVAT) compliance. Additional security precautions include Role-Based Access Controls, data encrypted at-rest and in transit, required Multi-Factor Authentication, and regular penetration testing.

Myth

Flock sells and/or shares customer data.

Fact

Your community owns 100% of your data and it will never be sold. Only your agency decides who to share your data with, not Flock. Flock Safety does not publicly release agency search data. Flock does not operate or support any public-facing searchable database of law enforcement lookups, and we do not provide license plate search histories to websites or third parties without the agency's knowledge and authorization. Other agencies who you share footage with have been responding to FOIA requests and sharing this search data.

Myth

My data is fed into a national database.

Fact

Each agency controls access to its own data. Agencies may choose to share information through a broader network, but nothing is shared automatically. Participation is opt-in, governed by defined agreements, and limited to lawful investigative purposes.

Myth

Flock cameras use facial recognition.

Fact

Flock cameras do not use facial recognition technology. Searches are based on vehicle characteristics, and not identity. Flock cannot recognize, identify, or track individuals. It is purpose built for specific public safety investigations, not to monitor people.

success_stories:
A technology that helped identify and arrest a homicide suspect within hours! Flock LPRs: let’s talk about the facts — and clear up the fiction. Ever since Flock Safety license plate reader cameras were installed throughout Yuba County in November 2022, they’ve helped deputies solve case after case. Stolen vehicles recovered. Suspects identified. Crimes connected. Real investigations, real victims, real results. But along with good technology comes some creative storytelling. So, let's clear a few things up. The cameras do NOT identify drivers or passengers : They do NOT spy on what you’re doing inside your vehicle: They do NOT record your road trip playlist: They are NOT used to issue speeding tickets or other traffic violations: They DO capture license plates and vehicle details to help law enforcement investigate crimes: They DO provide time-stamped data that helps connect cases and locate suspect vehicles: They DO help us keep our community safer. Think of them like a really smart notebook that remember vehicles, not people. We get it. New technology can feel a little “Big Brother-ish.” But if you’re worried about being tracked everywhere you go… your cell phone would like a word. The goal here is simple: protect our community using tools that help deputies solve crimes faster and more efficiently, while respecting privacy and staying within the law. Yuba County Sheriff's Department
